I'm continuing research for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (Confluence space key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net). This refines an earlier investigation — new information just surfaced that changes the target.

Background: A Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id 3193-47937) shows a boutique-related panel with "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE", a "CHOOSE A DATE" calendar grid, an "AVAILABLE TIMES" section with time-slot buttons, and a "CONTINUE" button. It's filed under a "Find in Boutique" grouping in the Figma layers panel. I'd previously hypothesized this was Booxi appointment-booking (a third-party appointment-scheduling vendor already documented for read-only appointment history in My Account, CRM-165-167), since nothing about "Find in Boutique" as documented (a pure per-boutique stock-check flyout, no dates/times) matched the screen.

**New information just confirmed by the project's frontend lead (a direct participant, not a guess):** this screen is specifically the **"Find in Boutique" → "Book a Fitting" flow/modal** — i.e., there's a specific named sub-flow called "Book a Fitting" that this calendar belongs to. I have NOT searched for the term "fitting" in any of my research so far (previous searches used "calendar", "date picker", "Booxi", "appointment" — never "fitting"), so this may surface documentation/tickets I completely missed.

Also newly revealed: a Figma comment thread on this exact screen, from a sticky note reading "Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar", authored by **Charmaine Lew**, posted "12 days ago" (so approximately 2026-07-30, given today is 2026-08-11), which tags/mentions **Kiera Rikard-Bell** and **Marcel Angelo N. Navarro** (the frontend lead) — with "1 reply" already in that thread (content not visible to me). Charmaine Lew is very likely a designer or BA/PM given she's leaving Figma design annotations.

Please research Confluence (space SFCC) and report back on:

1. **"Book a Fitting" / "fitting" directly.** Search broadly: "Book a Fitting", "fitting", "fitting appointment", "fitting room", "personal fitting", "made to measure", "bridal fitting", "styling appointment". Report any page found — title, ID, content summary, especially anything describing what this flow actually is (in-boutique tailoring/alterations fitting? styling consultation? something else?), what system backs it (Booxi? something else entirely?), and whether it involves in-storefront self-service booking or an external/chat handoff like the previously-found Inside Chat / INT-027 pattern.

2. **Charmaine Lew** — search for this name (confluence_search_user, then search content by/mentioning her) to establish her role (designer? BA? PM?) and find any pages she's authored, especially design-tracker entries or specs related to "Find in Boutique," "Book a Fitting," Booxi, or appointments.

3. **Kiera Rikard-Bell** — same treatment; establish her role and any pages she's authored or is mentioned on relating to this flow.

4. **Re-check whether "Find in Boutique" now has multiple sub-flows in Confluence** (not just the stock-check flyout previously found) — search the Design Tracker (258801666) and any PDP/Cart-adjacent design or requirements pages again specifically for a "Book a Fitting" row or sub-section that might have been missed because previous searches focused on stock-check/inventory terms rather than "fitting".

5. **Any newer/updated Booxi-adjacent content** — given "Book a Fitting" might be a specific appointment *type* within the broader Booxi/appointments scope (alongside "Personal Styling", which a previous pass found referenced in a "My Account – Services Page" context) — check whether a "Book a Fitting" concept is catalogued as a distinct appointment type anywhere, and whether it's tied to Booxi specifically or a different system.

Report back with page titles, IDs, and concrete content summaries/quotes for each question — I need to know whether "Book a Fitting" is a documented, scoped feature I simply hadn't searched for correctly before, or whether it's genuinely undocumented/new. This is read-only research — do not create, edit, or comment on any Confluence content. Keep the report focused and organized under the 5 numbered questions; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing an answer, not an end user directly.

## Research Report: "Book a Fitting" / Find in Boutique Investigation (Confluence space SFCC)

All searches performed via Confluence CQL/site search across the full SFCC space. No content was created, edited, or commented on — read-only throughout.

---

### 1. "Book a Fitting" / "fitting" — direct search

**Zero hits, across every variant tried:** `fitting`, `"Book a Fitting"`, `text ~ "fitting"`, `fitting appointment`, `fitting room`, `personal fitting`, `made to measure`, `tailor`, `alterations`, `bridal`, `styling appointment`, `appointment type`, `time slot`/`time-slot`, `calendar` (no relevant hits — only unrelated matches like "Scrum Meeting Cadence Calendar" and gift-card delivery-date pickers). I also pulled the full 200+-row **"04.1.11 Customers, Account, CRM Sync"** page (id `302022672`) directly and grepped it locally — the literal string "fitting" does not occur anywhere in it.

The only appointment-related **confirmed** requirements anywhere in Confluence are three rows in that same page:

| Req ID | Requirement | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| CRM-165 | "The system will display the customer's appointment history within My Account, sourced via the **Booksy** API" | Accenture | Confirmed |
| CRM-166 | "The system will treat **Booksy** as the system of record for all appointment data" | Zimmermann | Confirmed |
| CRM-167 | "The system will accommodate appointments as a section within the My Account area so that it can be incorporated **without structural redesign when ready**" | Accenture | Confirmed |

CRM-167's "when ready" phrasing is notable — it explicitly confirms only a placeholder/reserved section, not a built booking experience. The matching **"04.2 Design Tracker"** (id `258801666`) row — "Loyalty & Appointments" → "Appointments (Booksy)", Sprint 4 — has **no Figma link populated** and is Pending/Pending.

**Conclusion:** "Book a Fitting" as a self-service calendar/time-slot booking flow is not a documented or scoped requirement anywhere in Confluence. This is consistent with — and probably explains — Charmaine's Figma sticky note ("Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar"): there is no confirmed requirement or existing spec for this calendar, so she genuinely doesn't know if it's buildable/native or a vendor-supplied widget.

---

### 2. Charmaine Lew

Confirmed real Confluence user (account id `5d534dfedbb98c0d9c22ed4e`, `charmaine.lew@accenture.com`, `is_active: false` in the directory).

- **Role: Product Designer**, Accenture Onshore, **Melbourne** — per **"1.2 Team Overview"** (id `261586947`), listed under "Squad Oversight" (i.e., supports both delivery squads, not squad-specific) alongside Product Design Leadership (Marjo Kaszonyi, Jon Jackson) and fellow Product Designer Dennis Alvarenga.
- Attendee (ACN side) on the **PLP Workshop** in **"04.0 Requirements Workshops"** (id `342360068`): "ACN: Jasmijn, Bianca, Charmaine, Tash".
- Active named contributor in **"04.2 Design Tracker"** (id `258801666`) design-review notes: *"02-07: Charmaine to put was/now on PDP"*; *"01-07: is there a version of the billing address fields? Charmaine to make one version of checkout with this"*; *"24.06 → Hardi: might not be visible — Charmaine not to include in design"* (reCAPTCHA row).

No page authored *solely* by her turned up (creator/contributor CQL queries returned empty for both her and Kiera — this may be a tool/instance limitation rather than proof of authorship absence). But she's clearly an active Product Designer who works primarily in Figma and leaves her fingerprints as an action-owner in Confluence design-review tables rather than as a page author — consistent with her leaving a sticky note directly on the Figma file rather than a Confluence page.

### 4. "Find in Boutique" — re-check for sub-flows

Fully re-confirmed, now with the complete requirement set. **"04.1.8 Product, Catalogue and PDP"** (id `302776322`) contains PRD-018 (PDP CTA: *"Add to Bag and Find in Boutique as primary CTAs; Find in Boutique should open as a side out"*) plus **PRD-028 through PRD-039** (12 requirements), covering only: eligibility gating, modal header (thumbnail/name/colour/price), size pre-population, location search input, "Use My Location" geolocation with manual fallback, Google Maps directions, boutique result cards (name, address, distance, per-size stock status, hours, contact, live open/closed, map, "view more"), responsive modal, Enter-key search, configurable result limit. **Nothing in either place — or in "04.7 Component Inventory" (id `400195591`, which turned out to be a generic design-system primitives tracker: Banner/Button/Drawer/Footer, not a feature-flow tracker) — mentions dates, times, calendars, or booking.** There is no second, documented sub-flow under "Find in Boutique" anywhere in Confluence. ---

### 5. Booxi/Booksy — naming conflict and appointment-type scoping

**Significant, previously unflagged finding: Confluence itself is internally inconsistent between "Booksy" and "Booxi" as the vendor name for this same appointment integration.**

Pages using **"Booksy"**: "04.1.17 Third Party Integrations" (id `303890433`, sourced directly from the client's Functional Requirements Excel: *"Boutique Appointments | Booksy | The system will integrate with Booksy via MRT API connection..."*), "04.1.11 CRM Sync" (CRM-165/166), "04.2 Design Tracker", "Final Deliverables.pptx" attachment.

Pages using **"Booxi"**: "1.4 Third Party Overview" (id `261849101`), "2.5 PI 1 Planning Overview" (id `309690396`), "05.7 SFCC Architect Handover Checklist" (id `364544001`), "Technical Solution Design – PWA" (id `256835585` — MRT-mediated, credentials as MRT env vars, base URL "TBD"), "Zimmermann Detailed Architecture" whiteboard, and **"04.6 Consent Management — Business Overview"** (id `299433985`), which is the one place that frames it as an active **booking** tool rather than pure history: *"Booxi (boutique appointment booking) | Required | Functional booking tool."*

One page, **"8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)"** (id `264765445`), literally lists it as **"Booksy / Booxi"** side by side, suggesting whoever compiled it already suspected the naming ambiguity.

Most tellingly, **"Integration Reconciliation — Working Doc (Pre-Jira)"** (id `307134467`, a DRAFT reconciling the repo's `architecture.md`/`projectState.md`/`openItems.md` against Confluence's Integration Register) explicitly flags: *"Booxi | ... | — not in register at all | ... | Confluence register has no page/row for Booxi"* and lists it among *"Six repo integrations [with] no Confluence register page at all: Booxi, Transperfect, Google reCAPTCHA, GDPR cartridge, Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg."* This is an open, unresolved documentation gap already recognized by the project, not something I'm surfacing fresh — but the Booksy/Booxi spelling split specifically doesn't appear to have been called out as its own issue anywhere; the reconciliation doc treats "Booxi" as simply missing a register page, without noting that a *differently-spelled* version of apparently the same vendor already has extensive documentation under "Booksy."

**No appointment-type taxonomy exists anywhere** — I found no page cataloguing "Book a Fitting" alongside "Personal Styling" or any other named appointment type. My "Personal Styling" search only returned generic noise (SKU style codes, product styling images) — I could not independently reconfirm the "My Account – Services Page" reference from the prior pass under any phrasing I tried this time; flagging that as unconfirmed-today rather than re-asserting it.

**Synthesis (inference, not documented fact):** CRM-167's forward-compatible placeholder + 04.6's lone description of Booxi as a "booking tool" hint that a real booking capability is anticipated eventually, and that "Booxi" (not "Booksy") may be the vendor actually intended for booking rather than just history — but Confluence does not resolve this itself, and the Integration Reconciliation doc's own open questions leave vendor identity/scope unsettled. "Book a Fitting" sits ahead of all of this: it isn't tied to either spelling in any confirmed requirement.

---

### Bottom line for the synthesizing session

"Book a Fitting" is genuinely undocumented in Confluence — not a case of searching the wrong terms. Every plausible phrasing came back empty. What Confluence *does* establish: (a) the only confirmed appointment feature is read-only history via "Booksy" (CRM-165/166) with a forward-compatible-only placeholder (CRM-167); (b) "Find in Boutique" is exhaustively scoped as stock-check-only, no booking; (c) there's an unresolved Booksy-vs-Booxi naming split in the project's own documentation, with "Booxi" being the only spelling anyone has associated with actual booking (vs. Booksy = history/system-of-record); (d) Charmaine Lew is a confirmed Accenture Product Designer (Melbourne) actively working these design-tracker items; (e) Kiera Rikard-Bell has no Confluence footprint whatsoever, so her role is unknown from this source. The Figma "Book a Fitting" flow appears to be a design-stage concept running ahead of confirmed requirements — which lines up with Charmaine's own sticky-note uncertainty about whether the calendar is buildable in-house or vendor-supplied "out of the box."
